devdocs.title: API documentation
devdocs.sub: Read shipments and documents, receive events, and exchange EDI — over HTTPS, with scoped keys.
devdocs.authSub: Every /api/v1 request carries an API key.
devdocs.authP1: Keys look like niel_sk_… and are issued in your workspace under Integrations → API keys. The raw key is shown once — only its SHA-256 hash is stored, and it can never be recovered later.
devdocs.authP2: Send it as an Authorization: Bearer header on every request.
devdocs.authP3: Scopes are read and write. The public read endpoints below require the read scope. Write endpoints are coming soon.
devdocs.authNote: Create and revoke keys anytime in App → Integrations. Revoked keys stop working immediately.
devdocs.ep1d: List the key owner's shipments, most recently updated first.
devdocs.ep2d: One shipment by GTTID, master B/L number, or container number. Returns 404 when nothing matches.
devdocs.ep3d: Document metadata for the key owner's company (latest 100), including parse status. File downloads stay inside the workspace.
devdocs.respNote: Responses are JSON. Shipment objects include gttid, mbl_no, container_number, status, origin, destination, current_location, eta, and updated_at. Errors use { error, detail? } with HTTP status codes.
devdocs.whSub: Subscribe a URL per event in App → Integrations → Webhooks. Deliveries POST JSON within seconds, and every delivery is logged per endpoint.
devdocs.sigP1: Every delivery carries X-Niel-Event (the event name) and X-Niel-Signature: sha256=<hex>. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, keyed with your endpoint secret (whsec_…).
devdocs.sigP2: Compare in constant time and only accept bodies whose signature matches — then process the JSON { event, delivered_at, data }.
devdocs.ediSub: Trade EDI the way your partners already send it.
devdocs.ediP1: Paste or upload ANSI X12 in App → Integrations → EDI. The inbox auto-identifies 850 (purchase order), 856 (ship notice / ASN), and 810 (invoice), and parses each into structured data with header, lines, and totals.
devdocs.ediP2: Uploads are capped at 2 MB per document. Anything else lands as “unknown” with the raw text preserved for review.
devdocs.rateP1: No published per-minute limits — fair use applies. Planning sustained high volume? Talk to us first so we can provision for it.
devdocs.ctaSub: Keys live in your workspace — create one in under a minute.

bond.recContinuousD: One annual bond covering every entry at every U.S. port for 12 months.
bond.recStbD: One bond per shipment — flexible when you import only a few times a year.
bond.recNone: You may not need a bond yet
bond.recNoneD: Commercial imports valued at $2,500 or less usually don't require a bond (some regulated commodities are exceptions).
bond.whyCont1: With 4+ entries a year, one annual bond usually costs less than buying per shipment.
bond.whyCont2: Your estimated bond amount already reaches the CBP $50,000 minimum.
bond.whyCont3: You already use a continuous bond — renew or raise it before it lapses.
bond.whyStb1: With only a few entries a year, per-shipment bonds are more flexible.
bond.whyStb2: A single-transaction bond is typically sized around that one shipment's value.
bond.amtNote: Estimated per CBP guidance: 10% of duties / taxes / fees paid in the prior 12 months, minimum $50,000. The final amount is set during underwriting.
bond.finBody: You'll need financials upfront: CPA-reviewed statements or a tax return, plus a year-to-date internal balance sheet and P&L. Send us your assessment and we'll get you an individual underwritten quote.
bond.stbPriceNote: Single-transaction premiums are underwritten per shipment value — submit your assessment and we'll quote it accurately.
bond.saveTitle: Save your assessment, get human help
bond.saveSub: Leave your contact info and a licensed insurance agent will follow up on your bond application.
bond.done: Received! We'll be in touch shortly.
bond.fail: Something went wrong. Please try again or contact us directly.
bond.docusignNote: On the application, in the “primary Customs Broker / Freight Forwarder” field, enter your broker and add (Niel Insurance) after it so we can follow up on your submission.
bond.disclaimer: This assessment is an estimate based on public CBP guidance, for reference only — not an underwriting commitment. Bonds are underwritten by our surety partner; Niel Insurance Agency LLC is a licensed insurance agency arranging and servicing the bond.
bond.faq1q: Continuous vs. single-transaction — what's the difference?
bond.faq1a: A continuous bond lasts 12 months and covers every entry at every port. A single-transaction bond covers one shipment only. Import 4+ times a year and continuous is usually cheaper.
bond.faq2a: Commercial imports valued over $2,500 generally require one; some regulated commodities need a bond at any value.
bond.faq3q: How is the bond amount set?
bond.faq3a: CBP guidance: 10% of the duties, taxes and fees you paid in the prior 12 months, with a $50,000 minimum. Amounts above $50,000 require financials for underwriting.
bond.faq4a: No — applying is free, even if underwriting declines. Premium is billed annually, with a first-year special available.
bond.contPriceNote: The annual premium is quoted after underwriting — submit your assessment and we will get you an exact figure. Applying is free.

china.metaTitle: China to USA Import Guide | NIEL
china.metaDesc: Importing from China to the USA? Follow NIEL's 14-step checklist: HTS classification, duty calculation, Section 301/232, AD/CVD screening, PGA requirements, freight, insurance, customs bond, drayage and landed cost — every step linked to a free tool.
china.title: Importing from China? Start here.
china.sub: Fourteen steps from product idea to cleared, delivered goods. Every step links to a free NIEL tool — no account needed until you're ready to book.
china.stepsSub: Work top to bottom. Each step hands off to the next.
china.stepsNote: Duty figures are estimates from official 2026 sources — confirm with a licensed customs broker before filing.

0.d: Drop your commercial invoice or packing list into the Import Box. It reads the line items — SKUs, quantities, values, origins — so every later step works from real data.

1.d: Get the top-3 HTS candidates for each product with a confidence score and a plain-language reason. HTS decides everything downstream — duty, 301, PGA.

2.d: Look up the official 2026 USITC duty rate for your HTS — the base tariff every China shipment pays before surtaxes.

3.d: Most China-origin goods carry an extra 25% (Lists 1–3) or 7.5% (List 4A) under Section 301. See exactly which list your HTS falls on.

4.d: Steel, aluminum and copper derivatives face an additional 50% under Section 232. The estimator flags it automatically.

5.d: Anti-dumping and countervailing duties can exceed 100% on high-risk corridors like tires, solar panels and furniture. Screen against our curated watchlist.

6.d: FDA, EPA, FCC, CPSC and other agencies hold certain HTS codes at the border. Know your flags before you ship, not after.

7.d: Tariffs and CBP rules move fast. Follow the live regulatory feed — in English and Chinese — so a new proclamation never surprises you.

8.d: Request a freight quote for your lane. Tell us origin, destination and volume — a real person replies with a real rate.

9.d: Ocean marine and warehouse-to-warehouse coverage from a licensed agency. Get covered before the container sails.

10.d: Every US importer needs a customs bond. Apply for a continuous bond online in minutes through our surety partner.

11.d: Port-to-warehouse trucking, including heavy-weight containers. Request a drayage quote for LA/Long Beach, NY/NJ, Savannah or Chicago.

12.d: Short-term storage, transloading and fulfillment near major ports. Reserve warehouse space for your arrival window.

13.d: Put it all together — product value, duty, 301/232, HMF, MPF — into one landed-cost number you can price against.

adcvdchecker.rateNote: Cash-deposit rates vary by exporter/producer and administrative review. We never present a historical rate as the current rate.
